name: @local/dsh-oks
description: A Harness capability, not a wrapper for one model: whatever knowledge service (OKS) and data file a session's workspace declares in oks.json become seven native tools — search / references / info / check_intent / query / jaq_result / chart — turning a business question into rows read from that data file over a read-only connection, and into figures drawn on the server as SVG files in the workspace. oks_check_intent validates named intents and hands back a key for each accepted one; oks_query re-hashes that key before running, saves every success into a result file under the workspace's .data/, and returns only its dataSrc, columns and row count — the rows themselves are queried on demand with oks_jaq_result — a jaq/jq expression over the row array — so they stay out of the model context until asked for. oks_chart draws a figure — grouped columns, bars, lines, pie or area, all typeset by typst — into an SVG file in the workspace, from either a saved result (src, labelled "based on query results") or rows the agent supplies (data, "filled in by the agent"), and returns the markdown line that shows the figure in the reply. Search finds the keys of the vocabulary by name or description, references walks the reference graph backwards, and oks_info reads any node from the opaque key "index". va_ask consults a vocabulary helper the plugin owns (a top-level agent on the same preset and workspace, sharing the process-wide index, archived while idle): the plugin prepares it in one shot by putting the whole vocabulary and the working method into its system prompt — assembly sends no message at all — and after every answer collapses the question-and-answer into one fixed-text marker, so between questions the helper sees only the vocabulary, the method and the current question, while the session log stays append-only.
